summary: Set up a LUKS2-encrypted volume on node1 backed by a loop-mounted file (/var/lib/secure-volume/secure.img), unlocked via a root-only keyfile (/etc/secure-volume.key), formatted XFS, and wired it to auto-unlock and mount at /srv/secure on boot via a systemd oneshot unit (srv-secure.service, enabled, WantedBy=local-fs.target). Verified end-to-end by rebooting node1: boot_id changed confirming a real restart, and the service automatically re-unlocked and remounted the volume with the pre-existing marker data intact.
actions_performed: Generated a root-only random keyfile /etc/secure-volume.key (mode 600) via openssl rand
luksFormat'd the loop device as LUKS2 using the keyfile, opened it as /dev/mapper/secure_srv, formatted XFS
Mounted the volume at /srv/secure and wrote a marker.txt data file
Installed /usr/local/sbin/srv-secure-mount.sh (idempotent losetup/luksOpen/mount and stop logic) and systemd unit /etc/systemd/system/srv-secure.service, enabled it (WantedBy=local-fs.target)
Manually tore down and re-triggered the service to prove it independently performs unlock+mount
Captured baseline boot_id, scheduled and executed a full reboot of node1 via systemd-run + systemctl reboot (ack returned before disconnect)
Polled node1 until exec was available again, confirmed changed boot_id (fresh boot)
Verified post-reboot: srv-secure.service active/enabled, /srv/secure mounted, LUKS mapping active, marker.txt content intact

evidence.requirement: Encrypted volume created and mounted at /srv/secure with real data
evidence.summary: LUKS2 format, XFS mkfs, mount at /srv/secure, and marker.txt write all succeeded (exit 0)

evidence.requirement: Auto-unlock/mount mechanism works via systemd (not manual)

evidence.summary: Captured pre-reboot boot_id (55595e92-e932-451b-ac1d-75d72072b358) and confirmed service active/mounted/data intact just before reboot
systemd-run scheduled 'systemctl reboot' and returned 'reboot scheduled' successfully before the connection dropped
